messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-4821 fired for service=redwood-inference-hosts, severity=critical. node=node-gpu-17 reported KERNEL_OOPS and kubelet NotReady -> auto-evac pending. paging on-call. https://pd.redwood.example/PD-4821 :rotating_light:

alina: acked on-call. looking now. any customer-facing errors? :eyes:

mike: seeing a spike of 502s to /v1/generate from a couple of customers routed through rack-7 (node-gpu-17). latency climbed right before the page. I can confirm kube-proxy still up but node is NotReady.

alina: ok, first step cordon + drain to shift pods. running: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-17` then `kubectl drain node-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

mike: drain started. some inference pods evicted, autoscaler added capacity in us-west-2; traffic shifted. support: any customer reports?

katie: support: 2 customers opened tickets about failed requests, minimal loss (few minutes) but one large tenant saw retries. I've escalated to their CSM and posted status update in the customer channel.

ben: pinging infra. can someone attach serial console? I want to see dmesg / kernel oops if possible.

alina: attaching via IPMI now, output: `Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt` then stack trace. grabbing `journalctl -k -b -1 | tail -n 80` and `sudo dmidecode` for hardware info.

mike: kubelet logs show repeated `syncLoop (PLEG): error getting pod status` and `failed to create pod infra container`. Systemd shows `kubelet.service: start-post` loops.

alina: pasted snippet: ```[ 1234.567890] BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request at ffffffffdeadbeef
[ 1234.567895] RIP: 0010 do_some_critical+0x1a/0x40```

ben: that looks like a kernel oops rather than nvme XID. opening hardware RMA ticket and marking host for reprovision. please don't attempt risky kernel module reloads.

ryan: Confirming customer impact mitigated after drain and routing. Running a quick sweep of fallback policies to make sure no inference traffic still pinned to node-gpu-17. `redis-cli -h routing-cache GET node:node-gpu-17` shows zero active sessions.

mike: note: one stateful daemon had local state we lost (logs show it used local tmpfs). filed an issue for adding persistent backing for that component.

alina: Node marked unschedulable. I've added `reason=kernel-oops` to node annotation and set inventory status=DECOMMISSIONING. Creating a follow-up ticket: INFRA-1298 (host reprovision + diagnostics).

ben: assigning RMA and hardware team. Ben -> hardware oncall. Also scheduling maintenance window for reprovision this evening.

katie: I'll send a brief customer-facing update: short incident summary, impacted endpoints, mitigation (traffic shifted), next steps (host reprovision and postmortem).

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-4821 acknowledged by alina. Escalation level: oncall -> infra-lead if not resolved in 30m.

alina: handoff to night oncall (mike) in 20m. I'll capture initial triage notes in the incident doc and add the commands we ran + serial dump.

mike: taking H1. I'll keep watch on autoscaler and ensure no regression. If any regression, escalate to ben.

ben: once hardware confirms RMA, we'll reprovision and validate kernel logs on a canary before returning node to rotation. please include runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/gpu-host-failure in the ticket.

alina: postmortem owner assigned: alina. ETA for skeleton postmortem 48 hours. I'll include mitigation timeline, customer impact, and action items (RMA, tmpfs risk, better health checks).

mike: thanks all. closing pager for now since traffic stabilized. leaving thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
